chunks: Abdul-Wahid ibn Muhammad ibn Abdous (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us, saying: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn Qutayba al-Naisabouri narrated to us, from Hamdan ibn Sulayman, from Abdul-Salam ibn Saleh al-Harawi, who said: I heard Abu al-Hasan al-Rida (peace be upon him) say:

May Allah have mercy on a servant who revives our cause. I said to him: So how does he revive your cause? He said: By learning our sciences and teaching them to the people, for indeed, if the people knew the beauties of our speech, they would follow us. I said to him: O son of Allah's Messenger, it has been narrated to us from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) that he said: 'The one who learns knowledge to quarrel with the fools, or to boast with it before the scholars, or to draw the faces of people towards himself, then he is in the Fire.' He (peace be upon him) said: My grandfather spoke the truth. Do you know who the fools are? I said: No, O son of Allah's Messenger. He said: They are the storytellers from our opponents. And do you know who the scholars are? I said: No, O son of Allah's Messenger. He said: They are the scholars of the Family of Muhammad (peace be upon them), whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious, made obedience to obligatory and affection for them obligatory. Then he said: Do you know what is the meaning of his saying: 'Or to draw the faces of people towards himself'? I said: No. He said: He means by that, by Allah, the claiming of Imamate without its right; and whoever does that, he is in the Fire.

key_terms.لِيَقْبِلَ بِوُجُوهِ النَّاسِ إِلَيْهِ: To draw the faces of people towards himself
key_terms.لِيُبَاهِيَ بِهِ الْعُلَمَاءَ: To boast with it before the scholars

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Rida define 'fools' and 'scholars' in the context of using knowledge for boasting?
ai.summary: Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) elucidates that reviving the Ahl al-Bayt's cause requires mastering and disseminating their specific sciences, distinguishing true scholarly authority from mere rhetorical skill. He reinterprets Imam al-Sadiq’s warning about 'fools' and 'scholars' by identifying the former as opposing storytellers (qassa) and the latter as the Imams themselves, whose obedience is divinely mandated. Furthermore, he clarifies that 'drawing faces towards oneself' signifies the usurpation of Imamate, a grave sin leading to Hellfire, thereby linking epistemological authority with political and spiritual legitimacy.

en.basel-kadem: 1.	We were told by Abdul-Wahid bin Muhammed bin ‘Abdous, may Allah grant him mercy, that he said: We were told by Ali bin Muhammed bin Qutayba al-Naisabouri, from Hamdan bin Sulayman, from Abdul-Salam bin Saleh al-Harawi, that he said: I heard Abu’l-Hasan al-Rida, peace be upon him, say:

May Allah have mercy upon a servant who revives our cause. Then I said to him: So how would he revive your cause? He said: By him learning our sciences and teaching it to the people, for indeed, if the people were to know the beauties of our speech, they would have followed us. He said: Then I said to him: O son of Allah’s Messenger, it has been narrated to us of Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said: «The one who learns (some) knowledge that he might use it to quarrel with fools, boast with it before scholars or draw the faces of people towards himself, then he is in the Fire of Hell». So he, peace be upon him, said: My grandfather spoke true, so do you know who the fools are? So I said: No, O son of Allah’s Messenger. He said: Then he said: They are storytellers from our opponents, and do you know who the scholars are? So I said: No, O son of Allah’s Messenger. He said: Then he said: They are the Scholars from the Family of Muhammed, peace be upon them, whom Allah, Exalted and Glorious is He, imposed obedience to and obliged affection to. Then he said: Do you know what is the meaning of his saying: « or draw the faces of people towards himself»? I said: No. He said: He means with that, by Allah, the claiming of Imamate without its right; the one who does that, he is in the Fire of Hell.
